title: Women's Charter (Family Violence and Other Matters) (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Women's Charter (Family Violence and Other Matters) (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: NCSS domestic violence prevalence review
sections.summary: A 2019 NCSS review estimated about 3% of Singapore's population experienced domestic violence based on administrative data, ranging 3% to 20% self-reported.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In comparison, a 2019 review by the National Council of Social Service in Singapore estimated that about 3% of Singapore's population of men and women experienced some form of domestic violence based on administrative data, but this ranges from 3% to 20% based on self-reported data.

sections.label: NAVH helpline call increase
sections.summary: Since MSF's NAVH helpline launched in 2021, calls received increased from 8,400 to 10,800 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Since the launch of the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF)'s National Anti-Violence and Sexual Harassment Helpline, or NAVH, in 2021, the number of calls received has increased from 8,400 to 10,800 in 2022.

sections.label: INTRACS study on family violence
sections.summary: The MSF and NCSS INTRACS study suggested family violence tends to co-occur with negative life experiences and other factors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The Intergenerational Transmission of Criminality and Other Social Disadvantages, otherwise known as INTRACS study, conducted by MSF and National Council of Social Service (NCSS), suggested that family violence tends to co-occur with negative life experiences and other factors, such as prior contact with child protection and welfare or criminal justice systems and early marriage and parenthood before the age of 21.

sections.label: INTRACS PPO and child protection
sections.summary: The INTRACS study found children whose parents had contact with the PPO system were 7.63 times more likely to have child protective system contact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The INTRACS study which I mentioned earlier found that children whose parents had contact with the personal protection order (PPO) system were 7.63 times more likely to have contact with the child protective system.

sections.label: Taskforce recommendations progressively implemented
sections.summary: The taskforce's recommendations have been progressively implemented since the report was released in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Your unwavering commitment has helped to keep our families safe.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I am glad to share that the recommendations of the taskforce have been progressively implemented since the report was released in 2021.

sections.label: Family violence training and response team
sections.summary: Over 5,000 people were trained through Family and Domestic Violence Awareness Training, and MSF launched a 24-hour Domestic Violence Emergency Response Team in April.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Through the Family and Domestic Violence Awareness Training, more than 5,000 people across the people, public and private sectors have been trained to spot and report signs of family violence and we will continue to extend our training and outreach.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: MSF launched a 24-hour Domestic Violence Emergency Response Team in April this year.

sections.label: Possible standalone Domestic Violence Act
sections.summary: MSF may consider enacting a standalone Domestic Violence Act to enhance protection for persons in intimate non-familial relationships.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: MSF is prepared to consider the possibility of enacting a standalone Domestic Violence Act in the future to enhance protection for persons in intimate non-familial relationships.

sections.label: Financial abuse emerging issue
sections.summary: The Taskforce on Family Violence report states financial abuse is an emerging issue requiring further study.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: As pointed out in the report by the Taskforce on Family Violence, financial abuse is an emerging issue and requires further study.

sections.label: Younger survivors apply for PPO
sections.summary: The new section 60 allows younger survivors to apply for a PPO on their own.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The new section 60 allows younger survivors to apply for a PPO on their own.

sections.label: Stay Away and No Contact Orders
sections.summary: The new section 60B allows survivors to apply for a Stay Away Order, a No Contact Order, or both against the perpetrator.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: For better legal protection, the new section 60B allows survivors to apply for a Stay Away Order or a No Contact Order, or both to be imposed on the perpetrator.

sections.label: Protectors issue Emergency Orders on site
sections.summary: Under new sections 62 to 62C, protectors can issue Emergency Orders on site in high-risk cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Under the new sections 62 to 62C, protectors will be able to issue Emergency Orders on site in high-risk cases.

sections.label: Emergency Order additional orders breach arrestable
sections.summary: The Emergency Order may include a Domestic Exclusion Order, Stay Away Order, No Contact Order, or combination, and breach is an arrestable offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The Emergency Order may also include a Domestic Exclusion Order, a Stay Away Order, a No Contact Order, or a combination of these additional orders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: A breach of any of these orders will be an arrestable offence.

sections.label: Limit on Emergency Orders
sections.summary: Protectors may make up to four Emergency Orders against a given perpetrator within three months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: As a safeguard, Protectors will be limited to making up to four Emergency Orders against a given perpetrator within three months.

sections.label: Protectors apply for orders
sections.summary: New section 60 lets Protectors apply for PPOs, Stay Away, No Contact, Domestic Exclusion or Counselling Orders for survivors without consent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The new section 60 allows Protectors to make applications for PPOs, Stay Away, No Contact, Domestic Exclusion or Counselling Orders on behalf of survivors, even if the survivor does not consent.

sections.label: MSF family violence approach
sections.summary: MSF holds perpetrators accountable, so removal orders are only for exceptional high-risk cases, with alternatives like electronic monitoring considered first.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: MSF’s approach to family violence cases is that perpetrators, not survivors, should be held accountable for the violence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Hence, protectors will only apply for a removal order in exceptional, high-risk cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Other alternatives such as electronic monitoring of the perpetrator will be considered before removing a survivor from his or her home.

sections.label: PPOs with Counselling Orders
sections.summary: About 93% of PPOs issued from 2018 to 2022 were tagged with a Counselling Order.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: About 93% of PPOs issued from 2018 to 2022 were tagged with a Counselling Order.

sections.label: Mandatory Treatment Orders power
sections.summary: New section 60F empowers the Court to make Mandatory Treatment Orders against perpetrators under a PPO whose psychiatric condition likely contributes to family violence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The new section 60F empowers the Court to make Mandatory Treatment Orders against perpetrators under a PPO whose psychiatric condition is likely to be a contributing factor to the occurrence of family violence.

sections.label: Mandatory Treatment Order duration
sections.summary: A perpetrator under a Mandatory Treatment Order may receive up to 36 months of treatment, possibly residing in a psychiatric institution or treatment place.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: A perpetrator under a Mandatory Treatment Order may receive up to 36 months of treatment, which may include a requirement to reside in a psychiatric institution or a place providing psychiatric treatment.

sections.label: Higher fine and imprisonment
sections.summary: The maximum fine rises to $10,000 from $2,000 and the maximum imprisonment term increases to 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The fine will be raised to a maximum of $10,000, from $2,000 today, and the imprisonment term will be increased to a maximum of 12 months.

sections.label: Breaches of orders an offence
sections.summary: The Bill makes breaches of a Counselling Order or Mandatory Treatment Order an offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Second, the Bill makes breaches of a Counselling Order or Mandatory Treatment Order an offence.

sections.label: Stay Away and No Contact Orders
sections.summary: Survivors can apply for a Stay Away Order or a No Contact Order against the perpetrator, besides existing orders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In addition, to provide better protection, besides the existing Counselling Order and Domestic Exclusion Order, survivors can also apply for a Stay Away Order or a No Contact Order against the perpetrator.

sections.label: Protectors apply for orders
sections.summary: New section 60 lets Protectors apply for PPOs, Stay Away, No Contact, Domestic Exclusion or Counselling Orders for survivors without consent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The new section 60 allows Protectors to make applications for PPOs, Stay Away, No Contact, Domestic Exclusion or Counselling Orders on behalf of survivors, even if the survivor does not consent.

sections.label: Counselling Order scope expanded
sections.summary: New section 60E expands the existing Counselling Order to include other programmes, treatments and interventions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The new section 60E expands the scope of the existing Counselling Order to include other programmes, treatments and interventions.

sections.label: Protection and perpetrator accountability
sections.summary: The Bill strengthens protection of family violence survivors and enhances accountability and rehabilitation of perpetrators.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The Bill strengthens the protection of survivors of family violence and enhances the accountability and rehabilitation of perpetrators.

sections.label: Survivor consent for information publication
sections.summary: The amendment prohibits publishing or broadcasting identifiable information without the survivor's consent and the DGSW's approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: They should have greater control and say over the use of information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Therefore, I support the amendment's prohibition of the publication or broadcast of identifiable information, unless with the survivor's consent and the approval of the Director General of Social Welfare, or DGSW, in short.

sections.label: Re-offenders identification and public harm
sections.summary: The speaker agrees identification may protect the perpetrator, but asks that re-offenders be considered more seriously for identification due to public harm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: There is an argument that doing so may lead to the identification of the survivor and, hence, the perpetrator's name would also be protected unless with the survivor's consent and the DGSW's approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I agree with this in general, but I would ask that the re-offenders be considered more seriously for identification because of the element of public harm.

sections.label: DGSW duties and DVERT powers
sections.summary: The Bill gives the DGSW heavier duties, sets up a 24-hour DVERT issuing emergency orders, and lets the Court issue Stay Away Orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: As a result, however, the DGSW's office today, and going forward, is now entrusted with a lot more heavier responsibilities and duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: So, we need to also ensure that this office of the DGSW is properly resourced and supported so that this important work can also be carried out properly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Among the key changes brought about by the Bill is the setting up of a 24-hour Domestic Violence Emergency Response Team (DVERT).

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: DVERT will be empowered to issue emergency orders at the scene to require suspected offenders to leave domestic premises immediately and stay away for up to 14 days, while the victim applies to Court for protection orders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In addition to the traditional orders, such as the personal protection order (PPO), expedited order (EO) and domestic exclusion order (DEO), the Court will additionally be able to issue "Stay Away Orders" to require offenders not to go to places where the victim will frequent, for example, workplaces.

sections.label: Workers' Party supports Bill
sections.summary: The Workers' Party supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Having considered all these, the Workers' Party (WP) supports the Bill.

sections.label: Protector position and appointment
sections.summary: The Bill creates a protector with powers to make emergency orders, remove individuals and apply for orders, appointed only by the Director-General.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill creates the position of a protector, who holds significant powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A protector can make an emergency order before a Court order is obtained, can remove an individual from their residence and can apply for protection orders and other family violence orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 65(2) provides that only the Director-General may appoint any person with suitable qualifications and experience as a protector.

sections.label: Electronic monitoring order
sections.summary: Section 60C(2) allows the Court to make an electronic monitoring order if necessary for an individual's protection or personal safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Section 60C(2) allows the Court to make an electronic monitoring order if necessary for the protection or personal safety of an individual.

sections.label: Updated family violence definition
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the updated definition of family violence under new section 58B covering physical, sexual, emotional and psychological abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And this has also evolved with the times and the use of technology, for example.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Hence, for starters, I appreciate the updated definition of "family violence" under the new section 58B, to cover physical, sexual, emotional and psychological abuse.

sections.label: Amendments strengthening victim protections
sections.summary: The amendments let protectors make PPOs for victims, issue emergency orders, lower the PPO eligibility age and define rehabilitative provisions on perpetrator contact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The amendments to strengthen protections of victims include the ability for protectors to make personal protection orders (PPOs) on behalf of victims for their safety, to issue emergency orders, lowering the eligibility age to apply for a PPO and better-defined rehabilitative provisions to instruct and prohibit perpetrators from having contact with victims.

sections.label: Lowering PPO application age
sections.summary: Lowering the PPO application age from 21 to 18 helps more young people seek help but excludes those below 18.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While there is merit in bringing down the age of an individual who can apply for a PPO from 21 to 18, allowing for a larger number of young individuals to seek help, it discounts younger individuals below the age of 18 to take actions to cure a dire situation.

sections.label: Family violence cases and public education
sections.summary: In 2022 MSF investigated 2,254 new family violence cases and the helpline received 10,800 calls, with more public education and school training needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2022, MSF investigated 2,254 new family violence-related cases, while the National Anti-Violence and Sexual Harassment Helpline received 10,800 calls for assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: More can be done when it comes to public education in building awareness of what constitutes family violence and abuse and to encourage Singaporeans who witness family violence to reach out for assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Schools, in particular, should provide greater training and resources to help teachers and staff better identify signs of domestic violence in children.

sections.label: Support for domestic violence survivors
sections.summary: The speaker asks how to give psychological safety and support, calling for safe accommodation, timely response and long-term financial, housing, employment and immigration help for survivors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: How can we provide a level of psychological safety and support to those suffering in silence, such that they are willing to step out of their fears and to bring attention to their situation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We must recognise that there is an acute need for safe accommodation and timely response once the domestic violence report has been reported to the Police or once the PPO has been filed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In this regard, there should also be a range of long-term support and resources made accessible for survivors, beyond short-term responses to the family crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: These include access to financial and non-financial forms of assistance, such as access to housing, when they have no relatives to turn to for help, timely employment assistance and immigration support.

sections.label: Protectors applying for victims' PPOs
sections.summary: The Bill lets the Director-General of Social Welfare appoint protectors to apply for PPOs for reluctant victims, and the speaker asks if this covers those below 18 or mentally incapacitated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Under the new amendment, for victims reluctant to report their assailants, the Bill allows the Director-General of Social Welfare to appoint protectors to apply for the necessary PPOs on their behalf as well as to seek the appropriate orders as the protector deems fit to best protect the victim from further harm.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In this regard, I wish to inquire whether such empowerment also applies to victims who are willing but unable to apply due to factors such as age – those that are below 18 – or mental incapacity.

sections.label: Court powers for protective orders
sections.summary: The new regime gives the Court additional powers to issue orders such as domestic exclusion, Stay Away or No Contact orders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Under the new regime, the Court is given additional powers to issue orders such as domestic exclusion – a Stay Away or No Contact order.

sections.label: Concern about system abuse
sections.summary: The speaker asks how to ensure the new system is not abused by estranged spouses depriving the other of access to children during divorce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: While I am supportive of this new system, how can we ensure that it will not be abused by estranged spouses who are seeking to deprive the other of access to their children while they are in the midst of or in the aftermath of a bitter divorce proceeding?

sections.label: Urging victims to seek help
sections.summary: The speaker urges victims to come forward, warns against using PPOs for custody, and supports the reform Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: To those victims out there who are still suffering in silence, hoping that their situation will eventually improve for the better, I urge you to come forward and seek help.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: To those who think that by obtaining a PPO, it will increase your chance to obtain sole custody, care and control rights of your children, I urge you to think twice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Avenues to seek help for family protection under the Women's Charter should be seen as a shield and not as a sword.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the clarifications and suggestions I have raised earlier, I stand in support of this reform Bill.

sections.label: Protectors and emergency orders
sections.summary: The Bill lets protectors apply for PPOs on survivors' behalf and lets MSF's team issue emergency orders without going to Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For now, this Bill is yet another step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This Bill allows protectors to apply for PPO on the survivors' behalf even if these survivors do not want to do so on their own accord.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: MSF's Domestic Violence Emergency Response Team can also issue an emergency order without the need to go Court.

sections.label: Time limited emergency order
sections.summary: The Bill allows a time limited emergency order where there is imminent risk the perpetrator will commit family violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With this Bill, a time limited emergency order can be issued where there is an imminent risk and danger that the perpetrator will commit family violence.

sections.label: Threat sufficient for family violence
sections.summary: Under proposed section 58B(2)(a), a threat to cause personal injury or physical pain is sufficient for family violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under the proposed Women's Charter section 58B(2)(a), it is sufficient to constitute family violence if there is a threat to cause personal injury or physical pain, whether or not there is actual hurt or fear of hurt.

sections.label: Emergency order review and appeal
sections.summary: Emergency orders last 14 days, up to four in three months, with no apparent avenue for review or appeal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While an emergency order is stated to only have 14 days' validity, under section 62B(8), the protector has the power to issue fresh emergency orders, limited to four emergency orders in three months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding these extensive powers, there does not appear to be any avenue for review or appeal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can an individual subject to an emergency order apply to Court to cancel or vary the emergency order?

sections.label: Court powers for perpetrators
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes changes enhancing the Court's powers to order counselling and mandatory treatment for perpetrators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I hope he continues on this path and be an inspiration to others as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I welcome the changes to enhance powers for the Court to order counselling and mandatory treatments for perpetrators.

sections.label: Family violence harm definition
sections.summary: Family violence is defined by harm caused rather than perpetrator's intention, so survivors need not prove knowledge.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Mr Zhulkarnain is right that the definition of family violence looks to the harm caused by the perpetrator, rather than the intention of the perpetrator, and this is deliberate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Survivors should be able to obtain protection against harmful conduct without having to prove what the perpetrator knew or ought to have known.

sections.label: PPO applications by professionals
sections.summary: Social service professionals can already apply for PPOs for survivors below 21 or incapacitated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Yes, this is already the case, as social service professionals are already empowered to apply for PPOs on behalf of survivors who are below 21 years of age or who are incapacitated.

sections.label: PPOs for vulnerable dependants
sections.summary: Under new section 60A, the Court will not automatically issue PPOs for an applicant's vulnerable dependants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Under the new section 60A, the Court will not automatically issue PPOs for an applicant's vulnerable dependants.

sections.label: Perpetrator identity publication prohibition
sections.summary: The amendment prohibits publishing a perpetrator's identity only where it would likely lead to the survivor's identification.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The amendment prohibits a perpetrator's identity from being published, only where publication of his/her identity would likely lead to the survivor's identification.

sections.label: PPO duration and revocation
sections.summary: PPOs usually have effect indefinitely and stay in force until revoked.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: PPOs typically have effect indefinitely and remain in force until revoked.

sections.label: No appeals for Emergency Orders
sections.summary: No appeals will be allowed because Emergency Orders are temporary measures to protect survivors facing imminent harm.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Given that Emergency Orders are temporary measures intended to protect survivors facing imminent harm, no appeals will be allowed.

sections.label: Electronic monitoring for high-risk perpetrators
sections.summary: Electronic monitoring applies only to high-risk perpetrators in exceptional cases of suspected PPO breach with harm and no survivor self-protection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: As I shared in my opening speech, electronic monitoring will only be imposed on high-risk perpetrators in exceptional cases where there is reasonable suspicion that a PPO has been breached with harm inflicted on the survivor, and the survivor has not taken steps to protect himself or herself.

sections.label: Multi-pronged approach to family violence
sections.summary: Addressing family violence at its root requires a multi-pronged, whole-of-society approach with awareness, reporting, protection and rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: To address family violence at its root requires a multi-pronged, whole-of-society approach.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We must continue to: (a) increase awareness and strengthen societal attitudes against violence; (b) make it easier for survivors and the community to report violence and get immediate help; (c) strengthen protection and support for survivors; and (d) enhance rehabilitation for perpetrators.

sections.label: Protecting survivor and perpetrator identity
sections.summary: Section 63B protects the survivor's identity, and the Director-General will regard survivor consent as highly relevant to publishing identifying information.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Your work to stop the cycle of violence in families is well recognised, and this Bill would not have been possible without your contributions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I believe the amendments will go a long way in breaking the cycle of violence, to enable individuals and families experiencing family violence to heal, and ultimately, to help build stronger and more stable families in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: I just have one clarification in relation to section 63B of the new Bill which aims to protect the survivor's identity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: Since one of the objectives of the Bill is to rehabilitate the perpetrators to restore broken relationships, can I clarify if actually the provisions can also extend to providing the protections to the perpetrators in certain circumstances?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: As I mentioned in my earlier speech, the amendment prohibits a perpetrator's identity from being published only where the publication of his or her identity would likely lead to the survivor's identification.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: But if the survivor consents to the publication or broadcast of such information that could identify him or her, then the Director-General of Social Welfare will regard his or her consent as highly relevant.
